title: Daily load
purpose: Estimate a sampling day's mass load from an issued concentration and the corresponding daily flow.
summary: Use an eligible result from your current issued report and the corresponding sampling-day flow to calculate a daily load in pounds per day. Check how your permit defines the sample, flow, factor and rounding.

tasks.title: Calculate a daily load
steps: Check the [[Issued result]] against the sample and collection period that your permit specifies.
Enter the corresponding flow in [[Sampling-day flow]].
Select [[Calculate load]] to see the inputs and the daily load in pounds per day.

tasks.title: Check the source report
steps: Select [[Download issued PDF]] to read the report version that supplied the concentration.
If this version has been superseded, select [[current report]] and choose the result again.

good_to_know: The worksheet uses the conversion factor 8.34. Confirm that this calculation applies to your discharge and permit.
Non-detects, qualified results and field QC samples cannot supply a concentration here.
The worksheet keeps the issued digits and shows the product before permit-specific rounding.
The flow and calculated load are temporary. The worksheet does not add them to a report or submit a discharge monitoring report.

items.label: Report number, version and sample IDs
items.description: The header identifies the issued report, version, client sample ID and laboratory sample ID. The report number in the breadcrumb returns you to the current issue.

items.label: Current version / Superseded version
items.description: Only the current issued version of your own client's report can supply a calculation. If an amendment is issued while the worksheet is open, submitting the earlier version gives a notice. Select the result again in the current report.

items.label: Analyte / Reported concentration
items.description: The substance, reported value and original unit from this result. An unqualified, nonnegative detected concentration is required.

items.label: Matrix / Sample source / Field designation
items.description: The matrix must be Water or Wastewater. The sampling source and any field designation appear when recorded. Only field samples can supply a load. Use the source and location to identify the discharge your permit covers.

items.label: Collection type / Collected / Composite start / Composite end
items.description: Read the collection type and issued collection time with its recorded offset. When a composite start is recorded, both ends of the collection interval are shown. Check which daily flow corresponds to the sample.

items.label: Collection location
items.description: The place recorded for the sample at issue. An empty location appears as Not recorded.

items.label: Concentration in mg/L
items.description: For micrograms per liter (ug/L, µg/L or μg/L), the worksheet divides the issued concentration by 1,000. An issued mg/L result already has the calculation unit.

items.label: Download issued PDF
items.description: Retrieve the stored PDF of this exact version, including a superseded version. It is the report of record.

sections.title: Flow and calculation

items.label: Sampling-day flow
items.description: Enter the daily flow corresponding to the concentration, in million US gallons per day (MGD). Use a nonnegative decimal with up to 14 whole digits and 10 decimal places. Omit units, separators and exponents. Invalid input stays in the form for correction.

items.label: Calculate load / Calculated daily load
items.description: Multiply the concentration in mg/L by the entered flow in MGD and by 8.34. The result and its units appear with the inputs. Zero flow gives a zero product. The permittee decides whether the calculation, flow, rounding and reporting treatment apply.

items.label: Daily load unavailable
items.description: Read the reason shown for the selected result. A field QC designation, missing collection date, unusable basis, missing evidence, non-detect, negative or qualified result can withhold the calculation. The worksheet requires a Proceed receipt disposition. It checks the issued result, preservation and applicable analytical and preparation batch QC for qualifications, including reported subcontract qualifiers.

items.label: Demonstration
items.description: This notice identifies synthetic data. Use these records to try the workflow only.

paragraphs: Changing the flow recalculates the worksheet for the same issued result. Calculations are temporary and leave the original observations and report unchanged.
